title: Attention prefill signal fusion and kernel-selection oracle
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: paged attention workloads experience variable tail latency and token cost because the runtime makes conservative, one-size-fits-all kernel and prefill decisions. When fragments are fragmented or sparsely resident across KV pages, naive prefetch or aggressive prefill causes cache churn, decode stalls, or excessive token-cost due to duplicated work. Conversely, conservative admission under-utilizes available GPU throughput and increases end-to-end latency for interactive users.

Objective: build a lightweight runtime "kernel-selection oracle" that fuses (1) per-request early signals (prefix length, beam settings, requested max_new_tokens, SLO hint) with (2) live cache telemetry (fragment density, residency heatmap, recent-touch score, fragment co-location likelihood) and (3) hardware/queue state (current microbatch occupancy, kernel queue length, memory pressure) to pick: (A) the kernel variant (dense fused-kernel vs. sparse-friendly microkernel vs. two-step prefill+decode), and (B) a prefill urgency + pacing policy that shapes prefill admission to maximize throughput while minimizing tail-degrading cache writes.

Scope: implement signal fusion, a scoring function for prefill urgency, a pluggable kernel-selection API in the runtime, and a traffic-sim experiment harness that validates tradeoffs against existing heuristics. Focus specifically on paged attention and KV cache allocation/eviction interplay (we do NOT change LLM model weights or attention math).
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile end-to-end decode latency improvement >= 10% on synthetic 32k-sequence interactive traces with mixed short/long prefixes compared to baseline heuristics
Token cost (GPU cycles) no worse than baseline (+/- 3%) on peak load scenarios; for steady-state QPS with high fragment reuse, token cost should improve by >= 5%
No regression in decode error rates or correctness for production prompt suites (run against runtime-qa/prefill-regression)
Runtime exposes observability: per-request selected kernel, prefill-score, and prefill-admission decision; dashboard panels created alongside rollout
technical_notes: Signal inputs: prefix_token_count (int), requested_new_tokens (int), user_slo_ms_hint (optional float), fragment_touch_count (recent 1m/5m), fragment_density (float 0..1), co_location_probability (float 0..1), current_mem_pressure_pct
Score composition: linear combination with decay terms; final prefill_score in 0..100. Hysteresis window (5-15 score) to prevent flip-flop under jitter.
Kernel candidates: fused-dense (high throughput when co-located fragments >= 0.8), microkernel-sparse (lower throughput but low mem amplification), two-stage-prefill (aggressive prefetch then decode)
Admission control: token-budgeting per-GPU epoch. Prefill requests acquire soft credits; credits replenished based on observed decode-latency headroom to avoid head-of-line blocking.
Data collection: add per-fragment last_touch_ts, last_prefill_ts, resident_shard_id, and a lightweight bloom for co-location hints. Track decode stalls and backpressure metrics in admin telemetry.

Hot path performance: signal fusion must be <100ns on hot path; implement as a compact C++ struct + JIT-inlined scoring function with fallback to default heuristic if insufficient telemetry available.
Compatibility: kernel API must accept 'selection_hint' metadata on request to ensure Dedicated/Private clusters can opt-out during initial rollout.
implementation_plan: Spike: build a simulator (python harness) that replays production access traces and evaluates candidate scoring functions (1 week)
Runtime: add kernel-selection oracle interface and scoring code in runtime core (C++) + unit tests (2 weeks)
Instrumentation: emit per-request selection events to tracing pipeline and add metrics (prefill_score, admitted_prefill, selected_kernel) (3 days)
Microbatcher changes: add co-placement hint so kernels can group fragments predicted to be co-located (1 week)
Integration test: run against runtime-qa with the regression prompt suite and the synthetic 32k-seq trace (3 days)
Canary rollout: 5% traffic for hosted API with fallback to baseline heuristic on miss, monitor dashboards for 72h (3 days)
Ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% contingent on metrics and no regression detected (1 week total pacing)
Postmortem & tuning: collect results and iterate on scoring weights and hysteresis thresholds (ongoing)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: oracle misprediction could increase tail latency — mitigate with conservative default and automatic fallback to baseline if tail-latency delta > 2x within a rolling window
Risk: added telemetry increases hot-path overhead — mitigate by ensuring scoring path is extremely compact and feature-gating to enable/disable per deployment
Risk: prefill admission starvation for some tenants under global crediting — mitigate by tenant-weighted credits and emergency override for interactive SLOs
Risk: co-location hints may be stale causing ineffective microbatching — mitigate with short freshness TTL and prefer recent-touch signals over static co-location when stale
experiments: Sim A: baseline heuristic vs. linear-scoring oracle on replayed 7-day production trace (measure p50/p95/p99 latency and GPU token cycles)
Sim B: ablate co-location probability feature to validate its signal value
Live Canary: 5% traffic with oracle enabled + automatic rollback trigger on p99 latency increase > 5% over baseline
Admission tuning sweep: vary soft-credit size and hysteresis window to find sweet spot for mixed short/long request distributions
